query: I have $8,000 spread across three credit cards at 19%, 22%, and 24% APR. What's the best way to pay this off?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, NerdWallet, USA): The avalanche method — paying minimums on all cards and directing extra payments to the highest-rate debt first — minimizes total interest paid and is mathematically optimal for debt elimination.

Source 2 (2022, Investopedia, USA): The snowball method targets the smallest balance first regardless of rate; research shows it produces higher completion rates due to psychological momentum from early wins, despite costing slightly more in interest.

Source 3 (2023, Reddit r/personalfinance, USA): Community broadly favors avalanche for math-oriented people and snowball for those who've struggled to stay motivated — the best method is the one you'll actually stick to.

Source 4 (2022, Bankrate, USA): Balance transfer cards with 0% intro APR for 15–21 months can eliminate interest entirely during the promotional period — viable if you qualify for sufficient transfer limits and can pay off the balance before the rate resets.

Source 5 (2021, WSJ, USA): Debt consolidation loans at lower fixed rates (8–12% for good credit) can simplify repayment into one payment and reduce interest costs compared to revolving credit card debt at 19–24%.
atoms: perspective: Good-credit borrower eligible for balance transfer
perspective: Motivation-driven borrower needing quick wins
plausible_answers: Pay minimums on all cards and throw every extra dollar at the 24% card, since avalanche minimizes total interest.
Target the smallest balance first regardless of rate, since psychological wins keep most people on track better than pure math.
Transfer all balances to a 0% APR card and pay off within the promotional window to eliminate interest entirely.
